newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Hutmen sees 25 pct yearly net growth.
newsitem.headline: Polish Hutmen sees 25 pct yearly net growth.

text.p: Polish non-ferrous metals firm Hutmen SA, which plans its initial public offering in mid-year, expects its net profit to grow every year by 25 percent until the year 2000, the president of the company said on Tuesday.
"According to the management's forecast, (Hutmen's) net profit will rise by 25 percent every year by 2000," Henryk Orzechowski told a news conference.
This year Hutmen expects to net 7.6 million zlotys on 333-million-sales, up from last year's 4.9-million-zloty-net and 268.8-million-zloty sales.

The state treasury plans to sell 1,979,224 Hutmen's shares in a public offering in the second half of May. The company will carry out its initial public offering of 370,000 shares in late June and early July at the price set during the state's shares offering.
The shares held by the state will be offered at a minimum price of 30 zlotys. Hutmen currently has 2,474,030 shares.
Orzechowski also said the company planned to pay yearly dividends and suggested the management could propose earmarking about 40 percent of profits for payouts.

"We want to pay dividends, next year there will be a dividend, so far we were earmarking about 40 percent of net profit for bonuses for our employees so now it could be earmarked for dividends," he said.
Orzechowski also said the company considered the current 370,000-share issue too small for its needs and said the firm might carry out a new issue in 1998.
"Next year we might need a new issue...we wanted a bigger (initial public offering) but the current owner - the state treasury decided that the capital would be raised only by 15 percent," he said.
The company plans a 70-million-zloty investment programme in 1997-2000.
